lessons.title: Daily care routine in a layer house
lessons.html:
Daily care routine in a layer house

Commercial layers are hens kept to lay table eggs. A hen lays well only when she is calm, healthy, fed and watered every day. Your daily routine is the most important part of the job.

Morning round

  1. Enter through the foot bath and put on your house clothes and boots.
  2. Walk slowly through the whole house. Look and listen before you touch anything.
  3. Check that every drinker or nipple line has water. Press a few nipples to see that water comes out.
  4. Check that feeders or feed chains are running and that feed reaches the end of every line.
  5. Read the thermometer and check that fans, curtains and lights work.
  6. Remove dead birds and write the number in the house record book.

What healthy layers look like

  • Bright eyes and a red, full comb.
  • Active birds that eat and drink.
  • Clean feathers around the vent.
  • Normal droppings, not watery and not bloody.

Warning signs

Report to your supervisor straight away if you see many birds sitting with fluffed feathers, coughing or sneezing, a sudden drop in eggs, a sudden rise in dead birds, birds pecking each other until they bleed, or birds panting with open beaks and spread wings. Panting means the house is too hot.

Lighting

Layers need a fixed number of light hours each day to keep laying. Never change the light clock or switch off lights on your own. A sudden change in light can make hens stop laying. Follow the light programme set by the farm manager.

Be calm

Move slowly and do not shout or bang doors. Frightened hens pile up in corners and can smother each other. Fright also lowers egg numbers.

lessons.title: Collecting, handling and recording eggs
lessons.html:
Collecting, handling and recording eggs

Eggs are the product the farm sells. A cracked or dirty egg earns less money or must be thrown away. Careful handling protects the farm's income.

Collecting eggs

  1. Wash and dry your hands before you start.
  2. Collect eggs at the set times each day. In many houses this is two or more times a day.
  3. Pick up eggs gently. Do not drop eggs into trays from a height.
  4. Place eggs in trays with the pointed end facing down.
  5. Keep cracked, dirty and very small or very large eggs apart from good eggs.
  6. Do not stack trays so high that they fall.

Floor eggs and dirty eggs

Eggs laid on the floor or in the litter are often dirty and carry germs. Collect them separately and follow the farm rule for them. Do not wash eggs unless the farm tells you to and shows you the correct method.

Storing eggs

  • Take eggs to the egg room quickly.
  • Keep the egg room cool, clean and free of flies, rats and strong smells.
  • Keep eggs out of the sun.

Records

Every day write down in the house record book:

RecordWhy
Number of eggs collectedShows if laying is going up or down
Cracked and dirty eggsShows handling or nest problems
Dead birdsEarly warning of disease
Feed and water usedBirds eat and drink less when sick

A drop in eggs, feed or water is often the first sign of a problem. Tell your supervisor the same day.

Key points

  • Check water, feed, air and lights on every round.
  • Never change the light programme on your own.
  • Collect eggs gently, pointed end down, and keep cracked and dirty eggs apart.
  • Record eggs, deaths, feed and water every day.
  • Report sudden changes to your supervisor at once.

quiz.question: What should you do first when you enter a layer house in the morning?

options.text: Walk slowly through the house and look and listen

quiz.question: Hens are panting with open beaks and spread wings. What does this most likely mean?
How should eggs be placed in trays?

options.text: Any way, it does not matter

quiz.question: Who may change the light programme in a layer house?

options.text: Any worker who thinks it is too dark
Only the farm manager, following the light programme

quiz.question: Why must you record feed and water use every day?

options.text: Birds eat and drink less when they are sick, so it warns of problems
So you can stop feeding on some days
It is only needed for the bakkie log

quiz.question: Frightened hens can pile up in corners and smother each other.
Floor eggs are cleaner than nest eggs and can be packed with the good eggs.
Which of these are signs of healthy layers? (select all that apply)

options.text: Active birds that eat and drink
